To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the elderly have a higher risk of falling, (2) the risk increases with increasing number of comorbidities and (3) the risk of falling is increased by impaired balance and impaired lower extremity function.
the elderly are prone to falling due to a variety of reasons, that the foot and ankle play an important part in the control of postural balance, and that the foot can be a target for rehabilitation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the role of the lower limb, especially the foot, in postural control and locomotion, with particular reference to the elderly and the frail.
the development of new methods for the study of the dynamic behavior of a walking human.
the study of the effects of aging on the foot.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the elderly are not a homogeneous group and that there is a great variety of foot conditions in this age group.
the foot is an important part of the body and that the foot and its disorders are important in the elderly.
the foot is the most complex and most vulnerable structure in the human locomotor system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the foot and its function are the most neglected aspects of the elderly person.
we have shown that the foot and ankle are important for balance and mobility.
the elderly population is a very heterogeneous group and that the main problem is the loss of the functional reserve.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of aging on balance and gait are complex and multifactorial.
, while the majority of the participants were able to walk on their toes, there were some who were not able to.
we have a better understanding of how to improve the quality of care for older people with foot pain.
